classification.difficultyReason: Construct two zero-valued expressions by finding cancelling quantities among the cards while respecting operation precedence and the restriction against reusing a card.

content.prompt: Here are some number and operation cards.

spec.description: One horizontal row of five rounded-square number cards followed by four circular operation cards, all with white interiors.
spec.mathematics: Number cards in order: -2, 3, 4, 8, -9. Operation cards in order: +, -, multiplication, division. Different shapes identify number and operation cards.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied card values and operations remain visible in the question edition.

children.prompt: Choose any 3 number cards and 2 operation cards to go into these boxes. You can only use each card once.

spec.description: Three writable rounded-square number spaces alternate with two writable circular operation spaces.
spec.mathematics: Number, operation, number, operation, number. Each selected card is used at most once.
spec.answerVisibility: All five spaces are blank in the student prompt.

answer.worked: Choose the number cards $-2$, $4$ and $8$, and the operation cards $\times$ and $+$. Each card is used once.

inlines.answer: Depends on the cards you chose.

answer.short: Depends on the cards you chose.
answer.worked:
For the example $-2\times4+8$, multiply before adding:
$$\begin{align*}-2\times4+8&=-8+8\\&=0\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: Find two ways to make the answer zero.

spec.description: Two vertically stacked expression rows with matching horizontal alignment. Each row has three rounded-square number spaces alternating with two circular operation spaces.
spec.mathematics: Each row independently uses three distinct number cards and two distinct operation cards to produce zero.
spec.answerVisibility: Both expression rows remain completely blank in the student prompt.

answer.worked:
Multiply or divide before adding.
$$\begin{align*}-2\times4+8&=-8+8\\&=0\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}8\div4+(-2)&=2+(-2)\\&=0\end{align*}$$
Each expression uses three different number cards and two different operation cards.
